Huntington Bancshares Incorporated Reports 2026 Third-Quarter Earnings
Key Q3 Financial Data | Key Q3 Highlights
EPS of $0.33, unchanged for the quarter
Adjusted EPS (1) , which excludes the impact of Notable Items (as detailed in "Notable Items Influencing Earnings") was $0.38, down $0.01 from the prior quarter
ROTCE (1) of 14.6% and adjusted ROTCE (1)(2) of 16.6%
Net interest income increased 1% quarter-over-quarter; NIM of 3.25% was up 4 basis points driven by higher yields on investment securities and modestly lower overall net funding costs
Noninterest income decreased 8% quarter-over-quarter, largely due to lower capital markets fees and unfavorable equity valuation adjustments
Noninterest expense, excluding the impact of acquisition-related expenses, remained flat quarter-over-quarter
Average total loans and leases were down 0.4% compared to the prior quarter driven by declines in CRE and total consumer loans, partially offset by higher C&I loans
Average total deposits increased 0.2% quarter-over-quarter, with higher money market and interest-bearing demand balances, partially offset by lower time deposits
Maintained strong capital position, with CET1 risk-based capital ratio of 10.1% (3) , adjusted CET1 (1) risk-based capital ratio of 8.9% (3) , and TCE (1) ratio of 6.9%
TBV per common share (1) of $9.47 was down $0.18, or 2%, from the prior quarter, largely due to the impact of market interest rates unfavorably impacting AOCI
Repurchase d $100 million of common shares, bringing the total to $409 million and representing approximately 25 million shares repurchased year‑to‑date

"Huntington delivered a solid quarter, reflecting disciplined execution and continued business momentum across the franchise," said Steve Steinour, Huntington chairman and chief executive officer. "We are also seeing increasing benefits from our recent partnerships with Veritex and Cadence, and are achieving our targeted cost and revenue synergies. Our results reflect our disciplined growth strategy, in line with our aggregate moderate-to-low risk profile, and give us confidence that we are on track to meet our financial targets and deliver sustained growth in earnings, tangible book value and long-term shareholder returns."

Fully-taxable equivalent (FTE) net interest income for the third quarter increased $18 million, or 1%, from the prior quarter, driven by a 4 basis point increase in the net interest margin (NIM). The increase in NIM reflected higher earning-asset yields, primarily from reinvestment into higher yielding investment securities, and a decrease in average total borrowings, partially offset by higher deposit costs.

• Average earning assets decreased $3.3 billion, or 1% , primarily due to a $2.7 billion, or 16%, decrease in interest-earning deposits with banks and a $806 million decrease in average loans and leases.
• The yield on total investment and other securities increased quarter-over-quarter.

• Average interest-bearing liabilities decreased $3.3 billion , or 2% , primarily due to a $3.6 billion, or 16%, decrease in average total borrowings, partially offset by a $267 million increase in interest-bearing deposits.
• The average cost of total deposits increased 2 basis points quarter-over-quarter.

Fully-taxable equivalent (FTE) net interest income for the third quarter increased $567 million, or 37%, from the year-ago quarter, driven by higher average earning assets and an increase in NIM, partially offset by higher interest-bearing liabilities. NIM was 3.25%, up 12 basis points, reflecting a decrease in deposit costs, partially offset by lower earning-asset yields.

• Average earning assets increased $62.5 billion, or 32%, primarily due to a $52.5 billion, or 39%, increase in average loans and leases driven by loans acquired in the Cadence and Veritex acquisitions, in addition to organic loan growth.
• The yield on the total loan and lease portfolio was 5.84% , a decrease of 12 basis points.

• Average interest-bearing liabilities increased $48.5 billion, or 31%, primarily due to a $47.9 billion, or 35%, increase in interest-bearing deposits driven by deposits acquired in the Cadence and Veritex acquisitions, in addition to organic deposit growth.
• The average cost of total deposits was 1.90%, a decrease of 10 basis points.
See Page 4 of Quarterly Financial Supplement for additional detail.
Average total loans and leases decreased $806 million quarter-over-quarter.

• Average commercial loan balances decreased $303 million, primarily driven by an $854 million, or 4%, decrease in average commercial real estate loans, partially offset by a $553 million, or 1%, increase in average commercial and industrial loans.

• Average consumer loans decreased $503 million, or 1%, primarily driven by a $332 million, or 1%, decrease in average residential mortgage and a $311 million , or 2% , decrease in average automobile loans.

Average total loans and leases increased $52.5 billion, or 39%, from the year-ago quarter, largely due to the impact of the Cadence and Veritex acquisitions, in addition to organic loan growth over the last year.

• Average commercial loans increased $42.1 billion, or 54%, primarily driven by a $29.5 billion, or 48%, increase in average commercial and industrial loans and a $12.4 billion, or 116%, increase in average commercial real estate loans.

• Average consumer loans increased $10.4 billion, or 18%, primarily driven by a $8.7 billion, or 35% increase in average residential mortgage loans and a $1.6 billion, or 16%, increase in average home equity loans.
See Page 5 of Quarterly Financial Supplement for additional detail.
Average total deposits increased $413 million compared to the prior quarter.

Average total deposits increased $59.0 billion , or 36%, from the year-ago quarter , largely due to the impact of the Cadence and Veritex acquisitions, in addition to organic deposit growth over the last year .
• Average interest-bearing deposits increased $47.9 billion, or 35%.
• Average noninterest-bearing deposits increased $11.1 billion, or 38%.

• Capital markets and advisory fees decreased primarily due to lower underwriting and advisory fees.
• Other noninterest income decreased due largely to unfavorable valuation changes for strategic investment and other investments and a decrease in leasing revenue.

Compared with the year-ago quarter, noninterest income increased $94 million, or 15%. Excluding the impact of Notable Items, noninterest income increased $126 million , or 21%, over the year-ago quarter.
• The third quarter of 2026 included the full quarter impact of the Cadence and Veritex acquisitions.
• Payments and cash management revenue increased driven by higher cash management and interchange revenue.
• Capital markets and advisory fees increased primarily due to fees from the legacy business and the impact of Janney and TM Capital, in addition to higher syndication fees.
• Wealth and asset management revenue increased due largely to higher investment management and trust income.
• Customer deposit and loan fees increased driven by increases in loan commitment fees and the volume of personal service charges .

NPAs totaled $1.7 billion at September 30, 2026, an increase of $110 million from the prior quarter primarily driven by increases in commercial and industrial, commercial real estate, and residential mortgage NALs. Compared to a year ago, NPAs were up $901 million driven by increases in commercial and industrial, residential mortgage, commercial real estate, and home equity NALs, including NALs acquired as part of the Cadence and Veritex transactions.

The provis ion for credit losses was $123 million in the 2026 third quarter, a decrease of $9 million quarter-over-quarter and an increase of $1 million year-over-year. NCOs of $146 million increased $27 million quarter-over-quarter and $71 million year-over-year. NCOs represented an annualized 0.31% of average loans and leases in the current quarter, up from 0.25% in the prior quarter and 0.22% in the year-ago quarter. Commercial and consumer net charge-offs were 0.27% and 0.38%, respectively, for the 2026 third quarter.

The ALLL was $3.2 billion and the ACL was $3.4 billion at September 30, 2026. The ACL ratio was 1.75% at September 30, 2026, 3 basis points lower than the prior quarter and 11 basis points lower than a year-ago.

The tangible common equity to tan gible assets ratio was 6.9% at September 30, 2026, compared to 7.1% at June 30, 2026, with the decrease primarily due to a decline in accumulated other comprehensive income from higher market interest rates, as well as an increase in tangible assets driven by higher interest-earning deposits with banks, partially offset by current period earnings, net of dividends and share repurchases . Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) risk-based capital ratio was 10.1% at September 30, 2026, compared to 10.0% at June 30, 2026, with the increase driven by current period earnings, net of dividends, partially offset by the impact of share repurchases and modestly higher risk-weighted assets.

The provision for income taxes was $172 million in the 2026 third quarter, compared to $165 million in the 2026 second quarter. The effective tax rate for the 2026 third quarter was 19.3%, compared to 18.4% for the 2026 second quarter . The increase in the effective tax rate was primarily driven by higher non-deductible expenses in the current quarter.

Huntington Bancshares Incorporated is a $288 billion asset regional bank holding company headquartered in Columbus, Ohio. A top 10 U.S. commercial bank, The Huntington National Bank and its affiliates provide consumers, small and middle‐market businesses, corporations, municipalities, and other organizations with a comprehensive suite of banking, payments, wealth management, and risk management products and services. Founded in 1866, Huntington operates approximately 1,400 branches in 21 states, with certain businesses operating nationally. Visit Huntington.com for more information.

This document contains GAAP financial measures and non-GAAP financial measures where management believes it to be helpful in understanding our results of operations or financial position. Where non-GAAP financial measures are used, the comparable GAAP financial measure, as well as the reconciliation to the comparable GAAP financial measure, can be found herein.

Interest income, yields, and ratios on a FTE basis are considered non-GAAP financial measures. Management believes net interest income on a FTE basis provides a more accurate picture of the interest margin for comparison purposes. The FTE basis also allows management to assess the comparability of revenue arising from both taxable and tax-exempt sources. The FTE basis assumes a federal statutory tax rate of 21%.
In addition to capital ratios defined by banking regulators, the Company considers various other measures when evaluating capital utilization and adequacy, including:
• Tangible common equity to tangible assets,
• Tangible common equity to risk-weighted assets using Basel III definition, and

These non-regulatory capital ratios are viewed by management as useful additional methods of reflecting the level of capital available to withstand unexpected market conditions. Additionally, presentation of these ratios allows readers to compare the Company’s capitalization to other financial services companies. The tangible common equity ratios differ from capital ratios defined by banking regulators principally in that the numerator excludes preferred securities, the nature and extent of which varies among different financial services companies. The adjusted CET1 ratio differs from the defined CET1 regulatory capital ratio the Company is subject to by including the impact of accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) (AOCI) excluding cash flow hedges in the calculation of the capital ratio. These ratios are not defined in GAAP or federal banking regulations. As a result, these non-regulatory capital ratios disclosed by the Company may be considered non-GAAP financial measures.

Because there are no standardized definitions for these non-regulatory capital ratios, the Company’s calculation methods may differ from those used by other financial services companies. Also, there may be limits in the usefulness of these measures to investors. As a result, the Company encourages readers to consider the consolidated financial statements and other financial information contained in the related press release in their entirety, and not to rely on any single financial measure.
